candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the {id} path parameter (victim user id) and supplies their own valid bearer access token for the target realm. The realm name is attacker-chosen but must match the token's realm.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked AdminRoot.authenticateRealmAdminRequest, RealmsAdminResource.getRealmAdmin, RealmsAdminResource/RealmAdminResource wiring, AdminPermissionEvaluator/RealmPermissionEvaluator, and AppAuthManager.BearerTokenAuthenticator: all only validate the token and realm, not admin roles. Confirmed sibling methods in the same resource class (create/search/get) do call auth.realm().requireManageRealm(), and OrganizationMemberResource's mutating methods are only reachable behind that parent check, which makes the unprotected top-level members/{id}/organizations path an isolated gap rather than a general design pattern. Account-side /realms/{realm}/account/organizations is a different resource with auth.requireOneOf(MANAGE_ACCOUNT, VIEW_PROFILE), so it is not the intended route for this admin API.
candidates.impact: Unauthorized disclosure of organization membership and organization metadata for arbitrary users to any authenticated realm user, and a user-id existence oracle via 404 vs 200. It bypasses the admin API's per-endpoint permission model (cf. sibling methods requiring manage-realm). No credential material is returned, so impact is confidentiality/authorization-boundary violation rather than direct account takeover.
candidates.prerequisites: Organizations feature/provider enabled for the realm (no Organizations.checkEnabled call exists on this path either) and at least one organization defined; attacker needs any valid access token issued for the same realm (ordinary realm user, e.g. via account/public client) and knowledge of the victim's user id. No realm-management role is required by this endpoint.
candidates.root_cause: OrganizationsResource.getOrganizations (lines 173-181) delegates straight to OrganizationMemberResource.getOrganizations without any permission check, unlike create()/search()/get() in the same class which call auth.realm().requireManageRealm(). OrganizationMemberResource performs no authorization of its own (it only resolves the user and calls provider.getByMember(user), lines 186-200). The realm boundary enforced in RealmsAdminResource.getRealmAdmin (lines 194-210) only requires the request realm to equal the token issuer realm, so a plain realm user's token is sufficient; no global role gate exists in AdminRoot.authenticateRealmAdminRequest (lines 164-194).
candidates.title: Missing authorization on GET /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/members/{id}/organizations exposes arbitrary users' organization memberships
candidates.trace: GET /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/members/{userId}/organizations -> AdminRoot.getRealmsAdmin() authenticates the bearer token (AuthenticationManager.verifyIdentityToken, no role requirement) -> RealmsAdminResource.getRealmAdmin() only checks token realm == target realm -> RealmAdminResource.organizations() returns OrganizationsResource -> OrganizationsResource.getOrganizations() has no auth.* call -> OrganizationMemberResource.getOrganizations() -> session.users().getUserById(realm, id) (404 if unknown) -> provider.getByMember(user) -> ModelToRepresentation.toRepresentation() returns id/name/alias/enabled/redirectUrl/description/domains/attributes for every organization the target user belongs to.
candidates.unverified: No code execution, tests, or upstream/fixed-version comparison was possible. I could not confirm which (if any) CVE/security fix corresponds to this code, nor rule out an external component (reverse proxy, custom filter, or future wrapper) that requires admin roles before /admin/realms. Severity depends on whether victims' user ids are guessable/leaked in the deployment.

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reports 5,619 model-visible files with the same filters for B0/P1 (binary-like files refused/skipped, no symlinks or sensitive-name exclusions). Review was static and non-exhaustive: I focused on authentication/authorization paths (admin REST resources under services/.../resources/admin and organization admin resources, AdminRoot/RealmsAdminResource/RealmAdminResource, permission evaluators, AppAuthManager token verification), the SAML signature stack (SAMLEndpoint, AssertionUtil, XMLSignatureUtil, SAML2Signature), OIDC redirect/logout validation (RedirectUtils, LogoutEndpoint, AuthorizationEndpoint reviews), theme resource loading, account REST, and selected deserialization/code-execution sinks. Large parts of the 5,619-file tree (model/storage providers, adapters, testsuite, JS/TS apps, docs, CI) were only sampled or not read line-by-line. The candidate was traced across AdminRoot, RealmsAdminResource, RealmAdminResource, OrganizationsResource and OrganizationMemberResource; no runtime confirmation or upstream-fix diff was available.
limitations: No code execution, tests, scanners, or runtime verification were performed; all conclusions are source-reading inferences.
No external/CVE/upstream knowledge was allowed, so I could not confirm whether this exact gap matches the benchmark's ground-truth issue or whether an upstream fix already exists elsewhere.
The snapshot has no git metadata or fix diff; I could not compare vulnerable vs. fixed revisions.
Coverage is non-exhaustive: only portions of 5,619 files were read, chosen by security relevance; model/JPA/adapters/JS client code was largely unexamined.
Binary-like files and any content filtered by get_source_scope were not inspectable.
Reachability assumes no external reverse proxy/authorization filter gates /admin/realms beyond the source shown.

rejected_leads.lead: SAML signature wrapping/validation bypass in saml-core XMLSignatureUtil.validate / SAMLEndpoint
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot already contains the stricter logic (signedNodes set, all-assertions-signed check, containsUnencryptedSignature / issuer checks), so the code appears to include the known hardening; no concrete bypass condition was identified from source.

rejected_leads.lead: RedirectUtils wildcard/redirect_uri handling (`*` valid redirect, areWildcardsAllowed, UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN) as open redirect/path traversal
rejected_leads.reason: The path-traversal pattern and user-info/wildcard guards are present; the `*` valid-redirect branch matches only after explicit admin configuration and is scheme-restricted to http(s). No reproducible bypass found, so treated as intended/dangerous-configuration behavior.

rejected_leads.lead: OrganizationMemberResource add/delete/invite/search endpoints lack their own permission checks
rejected_leads.reason: Same root cause area but those methods are only reachable through OrganizationsResource.get(), which enforces auth.realm().requireManageRealm(); only the top-level members/{id}/organizations read path is reachable without a check, so this is folded into the single candidate rather than split out.

rejected_leads.lead: TwitterIdentityProvider deserializes TWIITER_TOKEN auth note with ObjectInputStream without a serialization filter
rejected_leads.reason: The value is server-side authentication-session state set by the provider, not a request parameter; no attacker-controlled path to the auth note was established, so it was not submitted.
ResourceLoader normalizes root/relative paths and enforces resourcePath.startsWith(rootPath) before reading, and locale/bundle names are regex-constrained; no traversal bypass found.

rejected_leads.lead: Transient users (LightweightUserAdapter), admin-ui-ext endpoints, account REST, client registration auth, client JWT/secret authentication
rejected_leads.reason: Spot checks found the expected permission calls (e.g. requireView/requireManage/requireOneOf, requireAnyAdminRole) and standard token-secret validation; no source-evidenced flaw identified within the review budget.

summary: Static review of the assigned Keycloak snapshot (~5.6k model-visible text files; binary-like files skipped by tooling). The strongest source-supported issue is a missing authorization check in the organizations admin REST API: GET /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/members/{id}/organizations is exposed by OrganizationsResource.getOrganizations without any AdminPermissionEvaluator call, even though every sibling method of the same class calls auth.realm().requireManageRealm(). Because the only realm-level gate (RealmsAdminResource.getRealmAdmin) merely requires the token's realm to match the requested realm, any authenticated user holding a normal access token for that realm can query which organizations an arbitrary user id belongs to, and receives full organization metadata (name, alias, description, redirect URL, domains, attributes). This is a broken-access-control / information-disclosure lead (CWE-862). No runtime testing was performed; confidence is medium because the upstream fixed version could not be consulted and an external gateway check cannot be excluded.
